Likoudis Legacy Foundation
Patron Report  ·  Spring 2026

A Foundation
Growing With Your Help

A personal update for those who have made this work possible.

Dear Friend of the Foundation,

Your support has made the last year possible. I want to give you a candid, personal account of where the Likoudis Legacy Foundation stands, what is launching in the coming months, and what your continued partnership means, practically, for the mission ahead.

I am finishing my Master of Arts in Catholic Studies at Franciscan University of Steubenville this May. The Foundation has been built in the margins — around coursework, around paid work, around everything else. What you have given is what has kept it from remaining a good idea on paper, and has enabled real progress.

What We've Built
likoudislegacy.com — Home
likoudislegacy.com — In Memoriam
likoudislegacy.com — Upcoming Events

The Foundation's new website — relaunched this spring at likoudislegacy.com — is the most visible expression of what we have been building: a permanent institutional home for ecumenical scholarship rooted in the legacy of James Likoudis. It hosts the Kydones Review, the Reading Circle, an event page for the Orientale Lumen Conference, the Fellows Program, a growing library of Dr. Likoudis's books, and an ongoing migration of his essay archive from his original site.

Coming This Spring
New Edition · Emmaus Road
Ending the Byzantine Greek Schism
Third Revised Edition  ·  James Likoudis
Foreword by Scott Hahn

The definitive Catholic treatment of the theological questions dividing East and West — papal primacy and the Filioque — is coming in a new edition with a foreword by Scott Hahn, including the fourteenth-century Apologia of Demetrios Kydones for union with Rome. We expect it available by end of May.

Demetrios Kydones is the reason our journal carries the name it does. A fourteenth-century Byzantine statesman and theologian who taught himself Latin to read Aquinas, he translated the Summa into Greek and wrote a formal Apologia defending his reception into communion with Rome — addressed to his own emperor, in his own tongue, at real personal and political cost. The new edition includes his Apologia alongside St. Thomas Aquinas's Contra Errores Graecorum, and several chapters by Dr. Likoudis addressing the contemporary difficulties that continue to impede reunion and pointing toward their resolution. Seeing this material reach a new generation is not incidental to the Foundation's mission. It is the mission.

We have also met with the PR team at the St. Paul Center for Biblical Theology and meet with their Marketing team next week. They plan to do significant marketing when the book releases. The timing could not be better: ecumenism has been a defining focus of Pope Leo XIV's early pontificate, and that attention will only amplify interest in a rigorous, faithful treatment of the East-West divide. The more that marketing is running on its own momentum, the freer I am to do interviews, appear on podcasts, and use that visibility to introduce people to Dr. Likoudis's broader body of work. That is a real opportunity for the Foundation — and one we want to be ready for.

The Reading Circle

The LLF Reading Circle launches May 29 on Zoom, led by Lizbeth Moncada. First text: The Divine Primacy by James Likoudis. Biblical and epistemic foundations of papal primacy. Open to all.

Lizbeth brings remarkable gifts to this work — intellectual seriousness, a warm teaching presence, and a genuine passion for the Likoudis legacy. For a body of thought that has spent decades largely out of print and out of circulation, a community gathered to read through it carefully and discuss it is no small thing.

Register at likoudislegacy.com/bookclub.html.

Active Programs
📖
Kydones Review

Call for papers open. Fall 2026 theme: Christian Unity in a Fragmented Age. Submissions to [email protected].

✝
Orientale Lumen

Conference on Catholic-Orthodox ecumenism, July 13–15, Baltimore. Archbishop Pace and Cardinal O'Malley confirmed. Full event details and registration at likoudislegacy.com.

✍
Tradition & Renewal

Daily Substack dispatches on Catholic intellectual life. Over 1,200 subscribers and growing.

The Fellows Program: Built, Not Yet Funded

Of everything the Foundation is building, the Fellows Program is the one that needs the most support to get off the ground. We have created several reading tracks and are exploring a certificate program. What we need now is a program director — someone deeply familiar with Dr. Likoudis's works — who can develop a full curriculum and direct fellows toward the pressing scholarly questions their work is best positioned to address.

The vision is concrete: fellows producing essays for the Kydones Review, translations, digital media, and other work that establishes the Foundation as a living center of Catholic ecumenical scholarship. That kind of output is what makes a foundation sustainable, attractive to grant-making organizations, and genuinely useful to the Church. Right now the program exists. Activating it requires stipends — and stipends require your support.

But the upside is real. We have roughly 1,200 people across the mailing list and Substack who are already engaged with this material. A fellow producing a well-designed course on papal primacy, or a video series on the Eastern Fathers, or a translation of a patristic text that has never appeared in English — that reaches an audience already there and already hungry. That is the kind of work that makes the Foundation a genuine center of scholarship rather than a publishing label, and makes it attractive to the grant-making organizations we are actively pursuing.

Your Support Compounds

What you have given has made a real difference. The Foundation has grown because of it — programs running, a journal taking shape, a conference confirmed, a community forming around work that deserves a wider audience.

I will be candid about where things stand. The Foundation has been, from the beginning, something I have run entirely in whatever spare time I have — around coursework, around freelance work, around job searching. It is not yet a paid career or a main job. It is something I believe in enough to do anyway. But we are reaching the point where that model has real limits.

The Kydones Review, the Reading Circle, the Orientale Lumen Conference, the publishing work, the Substack — each one is a serious program. Together, they require more capacity than one person can provide in stolen hours. The next step is bringing in a part-time intern or administrative assistant to ensure things actually move on schedule. That requires funding. Your support makes it possible for me to compensate someone for their time, to stop doing everything alone, and to free myself to do what I do best: write, speak, and build the intellectual case for what the Foundation stands for.

I graduate in May. The window that opens afterward — the conference, the book launch, the journal, the interview circuit — is the moment this all accelerates. I want to meet it with the capacity to do it well, not scrambling.

Give to the Foundation

I do not take lightly what it means that you have chosen to invest in this work. James Likoudis spent his life defending the unity of the Church — across the East-West divide, against the errors of his time, with firmness, clarity, charity, and patience. We carry that forward. Thank you for making it possible.

With gratitude and in Christ,

Andrew Likoudis
Founder & Chairman, Likoudis Legacy Foundation
Editor-in-Chief, The Kydones Review
M.A. Catholic Studies, Franciscan University of Steubenville (May 2026)
Website Kydones Review Reading Circle Give
